label: H.R. 4105

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Veterans Energy Transition Act of 2025 (VET Act of 2025) directs the Secretary of Labor to establish a grant program that helps transitioning service members, veterans, and their spouses find employment within the energy industry. It repeals older, expired authorities and sets up funding, eligibility rules, and reporting requirements for businesses that hire these covered individuals.

affected_groups.effect: They are eligible for assistance and preferences when seeking employment in the energy industry through participating entities.
affected_groups.group: Members of the Armed Forces, veterans, and their spouses

affected_groups.effect: Entities whose primary function involves energy generation, transmission, storage, distribution, or manufacturing critical components may receive grants to cover hiring and training costs for covered individuals.
affected_groups.group: Energy industry entities and small businesses

affected_groups.effect: The agencies must coordinate grant and transition programs, avoid duplication of services, and submit regular reports to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Department of Labor, Department of Defense, and Department of Veterans Affairs

key_provisions: Repeals expired authorities under sections 1152 and 1153 of title 10, United States Code, and establishes a new section 1152 grant program administered by the Secretary of Labor.
Provides grants to eligible energy-sector entities to reimburse costs incurred when hiring covered individuals, including expenses for training, licensure, recruitment, orientation, and relocation.
Sets limits on grant awards to a maximum of $10,000 per hired covered individual and no more than $500,000 per grantee in any fiscal year.
Gives preference in hiring to individuals facing employment barriers, such as service-connected disabilities, homelessness, involuntary separation, or residence in qualified opportunity zones.
Gives preference for grants to eligible entities that operate in qualified opportunity zones or are small business concerns.
Requires grantees to submit annual reports on fund usage, employee retention, satisfaction, salaries, and benefits, and to comply with audits and potential repayment for misuse of funds.
Authorizes appropriations of $60,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2031 to carry out the program, capping administrative costs at 15 percent per fiscal year.
missing_information: The total overall economic cost of the program beyond the authorized appropriations is not explicitly stated outside of the annual $60 million cap.

Specific details regarding the exact performance metrics or long-term targets for job placement success are not quantified beyond requirements for annual reporting and a final evaluation report due by September 30, 2030.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Veterans Energy Transition Act of 2025 (VET Act of 2025) directs the Secretary of Labor to establish a grant program that helps transitioning service members, veterans, and their spouses find employment within the energy industry. It repeals older, expired authorities and sets up funding, eligibility rules, and reporting requirements for businesses that hire these covered individuals.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a multi-year, federally funded grant program totaling $60,000,000 annually from fiscal years 2026 through 2031 to connect transitioning military members, veterans, and spouses with jobs in the energy sector, while establishing structured oversight, auditing, and reporting mandates.
